title: 流体力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Fluid Mechanics II
keywords: Laminar flow and transition 2.Turbulent flow 3.Viscous fluid 4.Friction, vortex and lift 5.Contribution to local community
educationalGoal: In this course, students will first understand the characteristics of viscous fluid and learn about flow in a pipe and flow around an object in the fluid. Then, students will learn about the mechanisms of drag and lift generation. With an emphasis on viscous fluid dynamics, which is the basis of actual fluid motion, students will focus on grasping the engineering and physical meanings while solving exercises on fluid flow concepts.
advice: This is a basic course in fluid mechanics. We will cover the following topics: 1. Outline of fluid dynamics 2. Outline of viscous fluid flow, laminar flow, transition, turbulent flow, and boundary layer 3. Analysis of viscous fluid flow, laminar flow in a circular pipe, and turbulent flow in a circular pipe 4. Flow in pipes, Bernoulli's equation considering loss, friction loss of pipe flow, losses of pipes, problems of piping systems 5. Force acting on a body, momentum theorem and drag, force, pressure resistance and frictional resistance acting on boundary layer and flat plate, flow and drag around cylinders and spheres, vortices, drag of objects with various shapes, fluid forces related to vortexes, and related vibration and safety design 6. Vortex and circulation, lift, and flow around a wing 7. Comprehensive problems: Report discussion and study meetings on specific issues (including regional contributions) in fluid dynamics. Express your understanding, ideas, and questions.
requiredKnowledge: Complete Industrial Mechanics I and II. Have knowledge of basic hydrostatics learned in Fundamentals of Fluid Mechanics I.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the mechanism of fluid losses and estimate them.
Be able to understand and calculate fluid forces, such as drag and lift.
Be able to set up a physical model for fluid-related phenomena and derive its basic equations.
Be able to apply basic equations to approximate an approach that closely conforms to natural fluid behavior.
Be able to understand the fluid engineering aspects of various fluid phenomena that can contribute to the commun
Be able to actively discuss issues and outcomes.

achievementLevels.ideal: Understand that fluid phenomena are governed by the basic equation of mechanics, and the induction of the basic equation of viscosity-related fluid phenomena, especially flow in pipes, can be completely realized. Explain completely the mechanism of fluid-related loss and calculate the flow in the pipe. Explain completely and calculate concretely the mechanisms of resistance and lift. Actively participate in questions and answers and also in essential discussions.
achievementLevels.standard: Understand that fluid phenomena are governed by the basic equation of dynamics. Describe and develop the method of induction of viscous fluid phenomena, in particular the basic formula of flow in a pipe. Explain simply the mechanism of fluid loss and calculate basic pipe flow. Explain and calculate concretely the definition of resistance and lift, as applied to, for example, wings. Participate actively in questions and answers.
